topics.title: Belgium: sharing power to stay together

learn.hook: How does a country where people speak three languages avoid a fight over who is in charge? Belgium found a clever answer!
points: Belgium is a small European country (smaller in area than Haryana) bordering the Netherlands, France, Germany and Luxembourg.
Its people: about 59% live in the Flemish region and speak Dutch, about 40% live in the Wallonia region and speak French, and about 1% speak German.

In the capital Brussels the picture flips: about 80% speak French and only 20% speak Dutch. The French-speaking minority was richer and more powerful, which the Dutch speakers resented, and tensions rose in the 1950s and 1960s.
Between 1970 and 1993 Belgium amended its Constitution four times so that everyone could live together. The country became federal in 1993.

The Belgian model: an equal number of Dutch and French-speaking ministers in the central government; powerful state governments not under the Centre; a separate Brussels government with equal representation; and a 'community government' for each language group dealing with culture, education and language.

example.q: Think it through: Why did the French speakers of Brussels agree to share power equally there, even though they were the majority in the city?
steps: In Brussels, French speakers were the majority (80%).
In the country as a whole, Dutch speakers were the majority (59%) yet accepted equal representation in the central government.
Each side gave up something where it was strong, so that it would be treated fairly where it was weak.
example.answer: It was a two-way deal: French speakers accepted equality in Brussels because Dutch speakers accepted equality in the central government.

learn.reallife: Brussels is also the headquarters of the European Union. Think of a class monitor team where one monitor is chosen from each section so that no section feels left out — that is the Belgian idea in miniature.

games.title: True or false: the Belgian model
items: The Belgian Constitution says the central government must have an equal number of Dutch and French-speaking ministers.
This equality ensures neither community can take decisions alone.
In Belgium, state governments are subordinate to the central government.
The state governments of the regions are not subordinate to the central government.
The community government is elected by people of one language group, wherever they live in Belgium.
Dutch, French and German-speaking communities each elect their own community government.
Dutch speakers are a majority in the city of Brussels.
Dutch speakers are about 20% in Brussels; French speakers are about 80%.
Brussels is the headquarters of the European Union.
This is one reason the Belgian arrangement in Brussels mattered so much.
Belgium solved its problem by making French the only official language.
Belgium shared power among all language groups instead of favouring one.

quiz.q: Which language is spoken by the majority of people in Belgium as a whole?
quiz.explain: About 59% of Belgians live in the Flemish region and speak Dutch.
steps: Asked: the majority language in Belgium as a whole.
About 59% live in the Flemish region and speak Dutch; about 40% speak French; about 1% German.
So Dutch is the majority language in the country.
French is the majority only in Brussels.
Answer: Dutch
quiz.mistake: Confuses the majority in Brussels (French) with the majority in the whole country

items: Dutch
French
German

quiz.q: In the city of Brussels, what share of people speak French?
quiz.explain: In Brussels about 80% speak French and 20% speak Dutch, the reverse of the national picture.
steps: Asked: the share of French speakers in Brussels.
In Brussels the national picture flips.
About 80% speak French and only 20% speak Dutch.
40% is the national French figure, not the Brussels one.
Answer: About 80%
quiz.mistake: Uses the national figure for French speakers instead of the Brussels figure

quiz.q: How many times did Belgium amend its Constitution between 1970 and 1993?
quiz.explain: Belgian leaders amended the Constitution four times in this period to build an arrangement where all communities could live together.
steps: Asked: the number of constitutional amendments, 1970–1993.
Belgium amended its Constitution four times in this period.
So the answer is 4.
quiz.mistake: Remembers that there were several amendments but not the exact number

quiz.q: What subjects does the 'community government' in Belgium deal with?
quiz.explain: The community government is elected by one language community and looks after culture, education and language.
steps: Asked: what the community government deals with.
Each language community elects its own community government.
It deals with cultural, educational and language-related issues.
Defence, currency and courts are not its subjects.
Answer: Cultural, educational and language-related issues
quiz.mistake: Thinks the community government is a full national government

quiz.q: Why did Dutch-speaking people resent the French-speaking community before the changes?
options: The French speakers were a majority in every region
The French speakers were relatively rich and powerful even though they were a minority in the country
The French speakers refused to live in Brussels
quiz.explain: The French-speaking minority was richer and more powerful; Dutch speakers got the benefits of economic development and education much later.
steps: Asked: why Dutch speakers resented French speakers.
French speakers were a minority in the country.
But they were relatively rich and powerful.
Dutch speakers resented this, and tensions rose in the 1950s and 1960s.
Answer: The French speakers were relatively rich and powerful even though they were a minority in the country
quiz.mistake: Assumes tension arises only when a group is a numerical majority

quiz.q: Which of these is NOT part of the Belgian model of power sharing?
options: Equal number of Dutch and French-speaking ministers in the central government
A separate government for Brussels with equal representation
State governments that are not subordinate to the Centre
Declaring Dutch as the only official language because Dutch speakers are the majority
quiz.explain: Belgium avoided majority rule by one community; making one language the only official language is what Sri Lanka did, not Belgium.
steps: Asked: which option is NOT part of the Belgian model.
Belgian model: equal ministers at the Centre, powerful states, a separate Brussels government, community governments.
Making one language the only official language is majoritarian.
That is what Sri Lanka did, not Belgium.
Answer: Declaring Dutch as the only official language because Dutch speakers are the majority
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the Belgian model with the majoritarian policy of Sri Lanka

quiz.q: Some special laws in Belgium need the support of a majority of members from each linguistic group. What does this achieve?
options: It lets the larger community pass laws faster
It removes the need for elections
No single community can take decisions on its own
It gives the German speakers a veto over every law
quiz.explain: Requiring a majority from each group means both communities must agree, so neither can impose its will on the other.
steps: Asked: what a majority from each linguistic group achieves.
A law needs support from both communities.
So neither community can decide on its own.
It is about mutual agreement, not speed.
Answer: No single community can take decisions on its own
quiz.mistake: Thinks power sharing is about speed rather than mutual agreement

quiz.q: In which year did Belgium shift from a unitary to a federal form of government?
quiz.explain: The last of the four constitutional amendments (1970-1993) came in 1993, when Belgium became federal.
steps: Asked: the year Belgium became federal.
The four amendments ran from 1970 to 1993.
With the last one, in 1993, Belgium became federal.
1970 is the start of the amendments; 1948 is Sri Lanka's independence.
Answer: 1993
quiz.mistake: Picks the starting year of the amendments, or a year from the Sri Lanka story

teach.ask: Gappu flutters in: 'Belgium has Dutch, French and German speakers. How did they stop quarrelling? Teach me the Belgian trick!'
teach.praise: Chirp! Equal ministers, strong regions, a fair Brussels and community governments — Belgium shares so it stays together!
teach.nudge: Nice! But who gets how many ministers in the central government? And what does the community government look after?

revise.summary: Belgium has Dutch, French and German speakers. Instead of letting one group rule, it amended its Constitution four times (1970–1993) to share power among all communities, and became federal in 1993.
focus: The language figures: about 59% Dutch, 40% French, 1% German in the country, but about 80% French and 20% Dutch in Brussels
The four parts of the Belgian model: equal ministers at the Centre, powerful state governments, a separate Brussels government with equal representation, and community governments
Why the deal was two-way: each side gave up something where it was strong
How the Belgian model differs from Sri Lanka's majoritarian policy
remember: Constitution amended four times between 1970 and 1993; Belgium became federal in 1993
Central government: an equal number of Dutch and French-speaking ministers
Community government: elected by one language group; deals with culture, education and language
Some special laws need the support of a majority of members from each linguistic group
traps: Don't confuse the majority in Brussels (French) with the majority in the whole country (Dutch)
Don't mix up the Belgian model with Sri Lanka's policy of making one language the only official language
Don't think the community government is a full national government

topics.title: Sri Lanka: the danger of majoritarianism

learn.hook: Two neighbours with different languages: one chose to share, the other chose to rule alone. Sri Lanka shows what happens with the second choice.
points: Sri Lanka is an island nation a few kilometres off the southern coast of Tamil Nadu. It became independent in 1948.

About 74% of the people speak Sinhala and about 18% speak Tamil. Among Tamils, Sri Lankan Tamils are about 13%; the rest are Indian Tamils, whose forefathers came from India as plantation workers in colonial times. Sri Lankan Tamils live mostly in the north and east.
Most Sinhala speakers are Buddhists; most Tamils are Hindus or Muslims; about 7% of people are Christians, who are both Tamil and Sinhala.

Majoritarian measures: a 1956 Act made Sinhala the only official language; Sinhala applicants were preferred for university positions and government jobs; and the Constitution said the state shall protect and foster Buddhism.

Sri Lankan Tamils felt alienated. They demanded Tamil as an official language, regional autonomy and equal opportunity. By the 1980s some groups demanded an independent Tamil Eelam in the north and east, and a long civil war followed, which ended in 2009.

example.q: Think it through: The Sinhala community was the majority. Why did ruling only in its own interest not bring peace?
steps: Majoritarianism means the majority rules as it wishes, ignoring the needs of the minority.
Tamils were denied an equal share in language, jobs and education, so they felt the government was not theirs.
When a group feels permanently left out, trust breaks down; in Sri Lanka this led to conflict and a civil war.
example.answer: Ignoring the minority undermined the unity of the country; majoritarian rule weakened, rather than strengthened, Sri Lanka.

learn.reallife: Imagine a school picnic where only the biggest group decides the food, games and timing every year. Soon the rest stop coming. Including everyone keeps the group together.

games.title: Sri Lanka: put events in order
items: Sri Lanka becomes independent (1948)
An Act makes Sinhala the only official language (1956)
Tamil groups demand an independent Tamil Eelam (by the 1980s)
The civil war ends (2009)

games.title: Belgium or Sri Lanka?
items: Equal number of ministers from the two main language groups
One language declared the only official language
Community governments for each language group
State to protect and foster one religion
Preference to the majority group for government jobs
Constitution amended four times to accommodate all groups
Demand for an independent state in the north and east
Separate government for the capital with equal representation

quiz.q: In which year did Sri Lanka become an independent country?
quiz.explain: Sri Lanka gained independence in 1948.
steps: Asked: the year of Sri Lanka's independence.
Sri Lanka became independent in 1948.
1947 is India's independence; 1956 is the Sinhala-only Act.
Answer: 1948
quiz.mistake: Confuses it with India's independence (1947) or the 1956 language Act

quiz.q: What did the 1956 Act in Sri Lanka do?
options: Made Tamil the only official language
Recognised Sinhala as the only official language
Made Sri Lanka a federal country
Gave equal status to Sinhala and Tamil
quiz.explain: The 1956 Act recognised Sinhala as the only official language, disregarding Tamil.
steps: Asked: what the 1956 Act did.
The 1956 Act recognised Sinhala as the only official language.
It disregarded Tamil, so it was a majoritarian measure, not power sharing.
Answer: Recognised Sinhala as the only official language
quiz.mistake: Assumes the Act was a power-sharing measure

quiz.q: What is 'majoritarianism'?
options: Sharing power equally among all groups
Rule by a group of military officers
Giving the minority a veto on all laws
The belief that the majority community should rule in whichever way it wants, disregarding the minority
quiz.explain: Majoritarianism ignores the wishes and needs of the minority; it is the opposite of power sharing.
steps: Asked: the meaning of majoritarianism.
It is the belief that the majority community should rule in whichever way it wants.
It disregards the wishes and needs of the minority.
So it is the opposite of power sharing.
Answer: The belief that the majority community should rule in whichever way it wants, disregarding the minority
quiz.mistake: Thinks any decision by majority vote is majoritarianism

quiz.q: About what percentage of Sri Lanka's people speak Sinhala?
quiz.explain: Sinhala speakers are about 74% and Tamil speakers about 18% of the population.
steps: Asked: the share of Sinhala speakers in Sri Lanka.
About 74% speak Sinhala and about 18% speak Tamil.
59% and 80% are Belgium's figures.
So the answer is 74%.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up Sri Lanka's figures with Belgium's

items: Sinhala
Sri Lankan Tamil
Indian Tamil

quiz.q: Who are the 'Indian Tamils' of Sri Lanka?
options: Tamils who migrated from Sri Lanka to India
Tamils whose forefathers came from India as plantation workers in colonial times
quiz.explain: Indian Tamils are Sri Lankan citizens whose ancestors were brought from India to work on plantations during colonial rule.
steps: Asked: who the Indian Tamils of Sri Lanka are.
They are Tamils whose forefathers came from India as plantation workers in colonial times.
They are not citizens of India living in Tamil Nadu.
Answer: Tamils whose forefathers came from India as plantation workers in colonial times
quiz.mistake: Thinks 'Indian Tamils' means citizens of India

quiz.q: Which was NOT a demand of the Sri Lankan Tamil political parties?
options: Recognition of Tamil as an official language
Equality of opportunity in education and jobs
quiz.explain: Protecting and fostering Buddhism was a majoritarian provision of the government; Tamil parties demanded language recognition, autonomy and equal opportunity.
steps: Asked: which was NOT a demand of the Tamil parties.
Tamil parties demanded Tamil as an official language, regional autonomy and equal opportunity.
Protecting and fostering Buddhism was a government (majoritarian) measure.
So 'making Buddhism the state religion' was not their demand.
quiz.mistake: Confuses government measures with the demands of the Tamil parties

quiz.q: Where were the Sri Lankan Tamils mainly concentrated?
options: North and east of the country
South and west of the country
quiz.explain: Sri Lankan Tamils lived mainly in the north and east, which is why the demand for Tamil Eelam was for that area.
steps: Asked: where Sri Lankan Tamils mainly lived.
Sri Lankan Tamils live mostly in the north and east.
That is why the demand for Tamil Eelam was for the north and east.
quiz.mistake: Does not link the demand for Tamil Eelam with where Tamils lived

quiz.q: What is the main lesson from comparing Belgium and Sri Lanka?
options: A majority community must always rule alone
Power sharing keeps a country united, while majoritarianism can break it apart
Language differences can never be managed
quiz.explain: Belgium accommodated its communities and stayed united; Sri Lanka's majoritarian policies led to distrust and civil war.
steps: Asked: the lesson from comparing Belgium and Sri Lanka.
Belgium shared power among communities and stayed united.
Sri Lanka's majoritarian policies led to distrust and a long civil war.
So power sharing keeps a country united; majoritarianism can break it.
quiz.mistake: Believes majority rule alone ensures stability

teach.ask: Gappu looks puzzled: 'In Sri Lanka the bigger group made all the rules. Isn't that fair? Explain what went wrong!'
teach.praise: Chirp! When the majority ignores the minority, trust breaks and conflict follows. Sharing is safer!
teach.nudge: Good! Which group was the majority, what did it impose, and how did the Tamils feel and react?

revise.summary: Sri Lanka's Sinhala majority passed majoritarian measures such as the 1956 Act making Sinhala the only official language. Tamils felt alienated, and distrust led to a long civil war that ended in 2009.
focus: The majoritarian measures: Sinhala as only official language, preference for Sinhala applicants in universities and jobs, and the state to protect and foster Buddhism
The demands of Sri Lankan Tamils: Tamil as an official language, regional autonomy, equal opportunity, and later Tamil Eelam
The lesson of comparing Belgium and Sri Lanka
remember: Independence 1948; 1956 Act made Sinhala the only official language; civil war ended in 2009
About 74% speak Sinhala and about 18% speak Tamil
Majoritarianism: the majority community rules in whichever way it wants, disregarding the minority
traps: Don't confuse government measures (like protecting Buddhism) with the demands of the Tamil parties
'Indian Tamils' are not citizens of India: their forefathers came from India as plantation workers in colonial times
Majoritarianism is not just any decision taken by majority vote

topics.title: Why share power, and the forms of power sharing

learn.hook: Power sharing is like a Diwali thali: many dishes on one plate, each with its own place. Why share, and how?
points: Prudential reason: sharing power reduces the chance of conflict between social groups and ensures political stability. It is wise in the long run.
Moral reason: sharing power is the very spirit of democracy. People affected by decisions have a right to be consulted and to live under a government they accept as legitimate.
Horizontal sharing: power is shared among organs of government at the same level — legislature, executive and judiciary. Each checks the others: a system of checks and balances.

Vertical sharing: power is shared among governments at different levels — a general government for the whole country and governments at the state or provincial level, and below them local governments such as panchayats and municipalities. This is federal division of power.

Power is also shared among social groups (like Belgium's community government, or reserved constituencies in India) and among political parties, pressure groups and movements (competition among parties, coalition governments, and interest groups influencing decisions).

example.q: Think it through: The Supreme Court strikes down a law passed by Parliament. Which form of power sharing is this?
steps: Parliament (legislature) and the Supreme Court (judiciary) are organs of government at the same level.
One organ is checking another, so no organ has unlimited power.
Sharing among organs at the same level is horizontal power sharing.
example.answer: Horizontal power sharing — an example of checks and balances.

learn.reallife: Your housing society has an elected committee, a treasurer who keeps accounts and an auditor who checks them. No one person can do everything — that is checks and balances in daily life.

games.title: Which form of power sharing?
items: Judiciary checks a law made by the legislature
Ministers are responsible to Parliament
Union and state governments have separate subjects
Panchayats and municipalities get some powers
Reserved constituencies for weaker sections
Several parties form a coalition government
Belgium's community government
Judges appointed by the executive can check the executive

items.text: Reducing conflict and ensuring stability is the ___ reason for power sharing.
Power shared among legislature, executive and judiciary is called ___ distribution.
Power shared among governments at different levels is called ___ distribution.
When two or more parties join to form a government, it is a ___ government.
Organs of government checking each other is called a system of checks and ___.

quiz.q: Which statement is a PRUDENTIAL reason for power sharing?
options: People have a right to be consulted on how they are governed
Power sharing is the spirit of democracy
Power sharing reduces conflict between social groups and brings political stability
Power sharing makes a government legitimate in itself
quiz.explain: Prudential reasons are about good outcomes — less conflict and more stability.
steps: Asked: a prudential reason for power sharing.
Prudential reasons are about good results.
Power sharing reduces conflict between social groups and brings political stability.
The right to be consulted and 'spirit of democracy' are moral reasons.
Answer: Power sharing reduces conflict between social groups and brings political stability
quiz.mistake: Confuses prudential (outcome-based) reasons with moral (value-based) reasons

quiz.q: Which statement is a MORAL reason for power sharing?
options: It reduces the chance of violence
It is the very spirit of democracy, since citizens have a right to be consulted
quiz.explain: The moral reason values power sharing for its own sake: in a democracy, those affected by power should share in it.
steps: Asked: a moral reason for power sharing.
Moral reasons value power sharing for its own sake.
It is the very spirit of democracy: those affected have a right to be consulted.
Reducing violence is a prudential reason.
Answer: It is the very spirit of democracy, since citizens have a right to be consulted
quiz.mistake: Treats every benefit of power sharing as a moral reason

quiz.q: Power shared among the legislature, executive and judiciary is called:
quiz.explain: These organs are at the same level, so sharing among them is horizontal.
steps: Asked: the name for sharing among legislature, executive and judiciary.
These organs are at the same level of government.
Sharing among organs at the same level is horizontal distribution of power.
quiz.mistake: Thinks 'vertical' refers to the separation of organs

quiz.q: Which is an example of vertical division of power in India?
options: Separate powers for the Union government, state governments and panchayats
quiz.explain: Vertical division shares power among levels of government — Union, state and local.
steps: Asked: an example of vertical division of power.
Vertical sharing is among governments at different levels.
Union, state and local governments (panchayats) each having powers fits this.
Courts reviewing a law is horizontal; alliances are among parties.
Answer: Separate powers for the Union government, state governments and panchayats
quiz.mistake: Confuses levels of government with organs of government

quiz.q: Reserved constituencies in assemblies and Parliament in India are an example of power sharing among:
quiz.explain: Reserved constituencies give socially weaker sections a share in power, which is sharing among social groups.
steps: Asked: what reserved constituencies show.
Reserved constituencies give socially weaker sections a share in power.
So this is power sharing among social groups.
quiz.mistake: Thinks reservation is a matter of division between levels of government

quiz.q: What is meant by 'checks and balances'?
options: The Centre checks every decision of the states
Each organ of government checks the others, so no organ has unlimited power
Courts decide which party forms the government
quiz.explain: Under checks and balances, legislature, executive and judiciary keep each other within limits.
steps: Asked: the meaning of checks and balances.
In horizontal sharing, each organ checks the others.
So no organ can have unlimited power.
It is not one level of government controlling another.
Answer: Each organ of government checks the others, so no organ has unlimited power
quiz.mistake: Thinks checks and balances means control by one level over another

quiz.q: When two or more political parties join hands to form a government, it is called:
quiz.explain: A coalition government shares power among parties — one form of power sharing among political parties.
steps: Asked: the name for a government formed by two or more parties.
When parties join hands to form a government, it is a coalition government.
It is power sharing among political parties, not a community government.
Answer: A coalition government
quiz.mistake: Confuses a coalition with Belgium's community government

quiz.q: Interest groups of traders, farmers or industrial workers influence decisions by taking part in committees or putting pressure on the government. This is power sharing among:
options: Political parties, pressure groups and movements
quiz.explain: Pressure groups and movements also get a share in governmental power by influencing the decision-making process.
steps: Given: traders, farmers or workers influence decisions through committees or pressure.
Interest groups and movements also share power by influencing decisions.
So this is sharing among political parties, pressure groups and movements.
quiz.mistake: Thinks only elected bodies share power in a democracy

teach.ask: Gappu chirps: 'Why should anyone share power? And how many ways can it be shared? Explain like I'm a baby bird!'
teach.praise: Chirp chirp! Two reasons — prudential and moral — and many forms: organs, levels, groups and parties!
teach.nudge: Almost! Can you give one prudential and one moral reason, and name a form like horizontal or vertical sharing?

revise.summary: Power sharing is good for two reasons: prudential (it reduces conflict and brings stability) and moral (it is the spirit of democracy). Power can be shared among organs of government, levels of government, social groups, and parties and pressure groups.
focus: Telling prudential reasons apart from moral reasons
Horizontal sharing (legislature, executive, judiciary) versus vertical sharing (Union, state, local)
Examples of sharing among social groups and among parties, pressure groups and movements
The meaning of checks and balances
remember: Prudential reason: reduces conflict between social groups and ensures political stability
Moral reason: power sharing is the very spirit of democracy
Horizontal: among organs at the same level; vertical: among governments at different levels (federal division)
Checks and balances: each organ checks the others, so no organ has unlimited power
traps: Don't confuse prudential (outcome-based) reasons with moral (value-based) reasons
Don't think 'vertical' refers to the separation of organs; that is horizontal
Reserved constituencies are sharing among social groups, not between levels of government
